Education · programme

Scholarship

Financial support for college students of Ramallah descent: up to four years of undergraduate support, extended through graduation for medical students, with named scholarships alongside the general fund.

Branch
Education · A ladder by age
Owning entity
ARFECF (Decision 3). afrp.org says the scholarship was established by the Ramallah Foundation and is run jointly with AFRP; the record follows the decision.
Shape
Award · flagship
Built in the Hub
Built

Who it's for

Students with direct lineage to the original Ramallah families, or sponsorship and approval; full-time at an accredited college; documented financial need; minimum 3.0 GPA.

The operating year

Jan-May: applications. 31 May: deadline. Jun-Jul: committee review and ranking. Jul: awards approved. Aug: disbursement. October and each year after: renewal reports.

The five rungs

RungFor this programme
HearThe household of a student in their final school years is told; lineage is checked once, through the family tree, and reused.
Show upAn application. Trying is showing up, and the applicant can see what has been received and what is missing.
Take partA continuing recipient, renewed each year; a missed renewal after a bereavement is not lapsed by silence.
Give or serveGiving back, from an alumni gift to a named scholarship; service and money rank the same.
LeadA seat on the Scholarship Committee, where conflicts with relatives are disclosed on the record.

Who runs it

The Scholarship Fund Committee under ARFECF; no designated officer may stand in for it (6.4.4). The committee enters its own award budget. Who approves the budget is an open question.

Money

ARFECF's Scholarship Fund, on ARFECF's books with ARFECF's receipts. The by-law's 5% cap is enforced; the 2015 Policy Statement's figures are shown inactive until the document is produced.

Hand-offs

Fed by lineage on the family tree and formerly by the HS Senior Award. Recipients get a free student membership and feed Project Hope, Leadership Ramallah, RBPN and the alumni programme.

What it needs

  • Scholarships (2019 plan)
  • Part of the youth pipeline from childhood to professional life (2019 plan)
  • Recruit 21-35 year-olds; programme alumni events at the Convention (2023 minutes)
From the platform
  • JP-020 open: the 5% cap versus the Policy Statement's 4% plus 1% waits on that document
  • JP-021 open: members elect a Scholarship Committee that no AFRP by-law constitutes
  • The ARFECF determination letter, needed for a receipt's exempt-status claim
  • Historic recipient import beyond the alumni match queue

Open questions

  • Who is the tax adviser who clears flagged disbursements?
  • What is the actual rubric, and how many reviewers per application?
  • How many named scholarships exist, and does each have written donor criteria?
  • Does the free student membership have an age or enrolment limit?
  • Who approves the budget: the committee within an envelope, or the Board?
